findings.claim: surfaceDelta compares raw working-tree bytes to git show blob bytes, so on a CRLF checkout (core.autocrlf=true) unchanged policy surface files are reported as changed.

findings.claim: policyBase decides isBoundary by branch name (branch != baseName) instead of spec-6's HEAD == base tip comparison; the L189-192 comment records this as deliberate.
findings.fix: none

findings.claim: session-mine.js adds a Drift stage, a model/effort tier override and --subagents forwarding that none of the 14 specs names.
findings.fix: none

findings.claim: Moving the worktree-table kind/base filter client-side made the header select-all checkbox (and any row checked before a filter change) select rows the active filter hides, so Remove / Remove Worktree acts on worktrees and branches the user filtered out of view. At base the filter was server-side (rows outside the filter were never rendered), so select-all could only ever pick visible rows.
findings.fix: Scope select-all to visible rows (tr[data-kind]:not([hidden]) input[name="branch"]) and have applyFilter uncheck every row it hides, then call refresh().

findings.claim: The shell consumers parse the presentation profile with sed and compare to the literal casual without stripping a trailing CR; .gitattributes does not pin settings/claude_code/presentation-profile.de.md, so a Windows/CRLF checkout yields audience 'casual\r' and sync_skills.sh takes the developer branch, while smine-nightly/run.sh never applies the casual defaults and passes 'language de\r' to consolidate.
findings.fix: Strip CR in every shell profile parse (sed ... | tr -d '\r' | head -1 in sync_skills.sh, smine-nightly/run.sh, cmd/bootstrap/run.sh), or pin settings/claude_code/presentation-profile.*.md (or *.md) to eol=lf in .gitattributes.

findings.claim: The casual jargon sweep moves displaced technical content 'into target/anchor/code/snippet fields', but a proposal's only anchor field is gate.anchor (internal/proposals/proposals.go:49-53), the ACDSL anchor regex smine-apply turns into the authored rule line; a reworded ID/path landing there makes step 4(a) append a rule governing the wrong files, against correctness-5 (gate fields never reworded). Same sink wording in the four dimension skills' L33 and smine-orchestrate L40.
findings.fix: Name snippet code or a technical fields[] entry as the casual-sweep sink instead of target/anchor (consolidate L51, the four dimension skills' L33, orchestrate L40), and forbid writes to gate.* and target during the sweep.

findings.claim: Step 3 promises a rule parked in settings.disabled.json never resurfaces, but reads it as the sibling of settings/claude_code/settings.json, which never exists; the config server parks rules in config.DisabledPath(~/.claude/settings.json) = ~/.claude/settings.disabled.json, so a parked rule granted again in later sessions is re-proposed.
findings.fix: Read parked rules from ~/.claude/settings.disabled.json (config.DisabledPath of the live settings), not from settings/claude_code/.

findings.claim: The gate prompt parameterizes the stylesheet via cssPath for check (1) on L77 but hard-codes 'style.css' for check (2) on L78, and the GATE_SCHEMA unstyled_input_types description (L43) repeats the literal; with any other cssPath the gate judges selectors and input types against two different stylesheets.
findings.fix: Interpolate the parameter on L78 (`no matching rule in ${cssPath}`) and make the L43 schema description stylesheet-neutral.

findings.claim: The new casual-presentation rule forbids file paths and rule/FACT/ACDSL IDs in change, but the same skill mandates machine-read change strings made of exactly those (eviction set projected="false" on <ID> / remove <ID> from <skill> context:, declare <entry-ID> in ... acdsl-context:), with no exemption like smine-permissions grants; smine-consolidate's casual sweep then rewrites change and breaks smine-apply step 4(d) dispatch. Same class in smine-skills L65.
findings.fix: Exempt the machine-read change forms (eviction set projected=/remove <ID> from, declare <ID> in, Workflows author workflows/<name>.js) from the casual rule in smine-context/smine-memory/smine-skills and from smine-consolidate's casual sweep, as smine-permissions does for its rule string.

findings.claim: On a casual install the step-4 casual lockout only sets disposition casual-locked; the proposal stays proposed with no autoApplyHeld, so step-5 auto-apply re-picks it every night, filling cap slots before the lockout fires and re-ledgering it each run; smine-skills never drops pre-existing locked entries and smine-consolidate can re-home them.
findings.fix: Apply the casual lockout at step-5 candidate selection (autoApplyHeld reason casual-locked, no cap slot), and have smine-skills reconciliation drop proposed edit entries that target locked skills on casual installs.

findings.claim: The acdsl policy guard only sees Write/Edit/NotebookEdit file paths, while the deployed settings template auto-allows Bash(cp *) under acceptEdits, so in a strict or gated repo an agent overwrites acdsl/policy.json with one Bash call and gets neither a deny nor a prompt (CheckPolicy still catches it at check time).
findings.fix: Register acdsl-policy-guard.sh under a Bash matcher too and, for tool_name Bash, deny when a command token resolves under the policy root to the self-management surface (strict: *.acdsl / acdsl/*); alternatively drop Bash(cp *) from the template allow list.

findings.claim: After an optimistic removal empties the table with no filter active, the page shows 'No agent branches matching the active filter.' although no filter is set.
findings.fix: Unhide wt-filter-empty only when kind or base is set: empty.hidden = visible > 0 || !(kind || base) || !document.querySelector('tr[data-kind]').

findings.claim: The two new pages set their browser <title> from untranslated literals — the Profile page ('Profile') and the sessions archive tab ('Sessions — archive', sessions.go:137) — so a German profile shows English tab titles while sibling handlers translate theirs.
findings.fix: Pass the Profile page title and the archive-tab title (sessions.go:137, as translate(language, "Sessions") + " — " + translate(language, "archive")) through translate(s.presentation.language(), ...).

findings.claim: stripFrontMatter guards `len(lines) == 0 || ...` after strings.Split with a non-empty separator, which always returns at least one element, so the len check is dead.
findings.fix: Drop the dead `len(lines) == 0 ||` term in stripFrontMatter; strings.Split never returns an empty slice.

findings.claim: The Windows prerequisites table lists the from-source winget prerequisites as 'Git for Windows, Go, jq', but install.ps1 now also detects shellcheck and winget-installs koalaman.shellcheck; the README copy disagrees with the script.
findings.fix: README.md:76 — list shellcheck alongside Git for Windows, Go, jq in the from-source (install.ps1) Needs cell, matching install.ps1:20.

findings.claim: EVID-002 and EVID-005 open with italic report-section labels while the rewritten EVID-003/004 open with bare 'Validated/Tested (feeds ...)' labels; four sibling entries use two label shapes.
findings.fix: Use one label shape for EVID-002..005, e.g. italic section labels on EVID-003/004 like EVID-002 and EVID-005.

findings.claim: The new skill's allowed-tools pre-approves Bash(jq *) but no step uses jq; the grant is dead and widens the pre-approved surface.
findings.fix: Drop Bash(jq *) from the smine-style allowed-tools line; no step runs jq.

findings.claim: The Build stage comment says '(pipeline, no barrier)', but L44 awaits the whole single-stage pipeline() before L58 starts Gate, so the stage is a barrier; the comment states the opposite of the code.
findings.fix: Use await parallel(...) as subsystem-grounding.js does and drop '(pipeline, no barrier)', or reword the comment to '(fan-out; barrier before Gate)'.

findings.claim: The L75 Rules bullet forbids colon forms in rule strings, but L47 of the same skill prescribes WebFetch(domain:<host>) and the live allowlist carries colon forms; a WebFetch or Skill(x:*) candidate meets two contradicting instructions.
findings.fix: Narrow L75 to Bash rules: 'space wildcards for Bash (Bash(x *)), never the legacy Bash(x:*) prefix form; WebFetch(domain:…) and Skill(…) strings exactly as the allowlist spells them'.

findings.claim: The gated verifier-allowlist check on the modified class (classViolations(..., "modified", true)) has no test; flipping it to false keeps the suite green while a gated branch can re-point an editable-scope rule to an unsanctioned verifier unreported.
findings.fix: Add a gated CheckPolicy case with base verifier_allowlist [gofmt] and a base registry holding gofmt plus other, where the working rules.acdsl re-binds editable ACDSL-GOLANG-100 to other; assert the 'binds verifier "other" outside the sanctioned set' diagnostic.

findings.claim: writeInstallEnv, the Windows writer of install.env, has no test, so nothing pins its KEY=VALUE output to the reader ExpandInstallMarkers (PEEK_CONTROL_PORT).
findings.fix: Add a //go:build windows install_windows_test.go that calls writeInstallEnv into t.TempDir(), chdirs there, and asserts config.ExpandInstallMarkers expands {{PEEK_CONTROL_PORT}} to the written port, plus an invalid-addr error case.

findings.claim: TestStartPeek's only mismatch case differs in both claude-home and codex-home, so the per-home identity check at main.go:248 is unpinned (&& -> || stays green).
findings.fix: Add TestStartPeek cases where exactly one of claude-home / codex-home mismatches the /healthz identity, each expecting false.

findings.claim: The template funcs t / langAttr / isDeveloperAudience now read presentationStore live so a Profile save takes effect without restart, but no test saves a profile over HTTP and then renders a page; reverting to a New()-time snapshot keeps the suite green.
findings.fix: Add a handler test: POST /profile {audience: casual, language: de} (stub sync scripts), then GET / and assert lang="de" and ">Übersicht"; switch back to developer/en and assert ">Overview".

findings.claim: The routine row's new Unscheduled branch ('not scheduled' cell at L28, data-reschedule="1" at L14) has no server render test; deleting either arm keeps the suite green.
findings.fix: Add internal/server/routines_test.go rendering tmplRoutineRow with routineView{Routine: routines.Routine{Unscheduled: true}} and assert 'not scheduled' plus data-reschedule="1"; a non-unscheduled unsupported view still renders 'unsupported schedule'.

findings.claim: handleWelcomeBootstrap's request-validation wiring (bootstrapEnv error -> 400 before any spawn) has no handler test.
findings.fix: Add a handler case: POST /welcome/bootstrap with since=banana, assert 400 and that s.bootstrap.pid stays 0.

findings.claim: spec-8 names the repos_test case 'add with reserved name default/archived -> rejected'; repos_test.go only posts name=default, archived is never sent through POST /repos/add.
findings.fix: Loop reserved-name-is-bad-request-before-git-init over {"default", "archived"}.

findings.claim: The gate's first-user-message-only marker scope is unpinned: every test transcript holds exactly one user line, so widening the jq to all user lines (incl. tool_result lines) keeps the suite green.
findings.fix: Add a test_skill_invoke_gate.sh case: transcript = plain first user line followed by a user tool_result line containing REQUIRE-SKILL:railroad-review; assert a Bash call stays silent.

findings.claim: spec-5 requires a stage-3 postcondition test (test_routine_worktree.sh extension, runbook stage3-postconditions), but no test drives the run.sh:327-339 block; deleting the dirty-tree check or swapping merged/kept stays green.
findings.fix: Extend cmd/tests/test_routine_worktree.sh (or a nightly harness with stubbed routine_run_claude) with stage-3 cases: dirty repo_root -> exit 70; merged run branch -> pruned; unmerged -> kept and .orchestrate-report surfaced.
